classification.difficultyReason: Translate both purchases into equations, choose multipliers for elimination and substitute back to find and label the two unit prices.

content.prompt:
3 pencil-top erasers and 2 clips cost $\$2.05$.

5 pencil-top erasers and 3 clips cost $\$3.20$.

What is the cost of 1 pencil-top eraser and what is the cost of 1 clip?

spec.description: Editable schematic pencil-top erasers and clips replace photographic cutouts. Three stacked rows retain erasers on the left and clips on the right, with unit-price question marks in the final row.
spec.mathematics: First row: 3 erasers and 2 clips. Second row: 5 erasers and 3 clips. Third row: 1 eraser and 1 clip, each labelled '= ?'.
spec.answerVisibility: Only object counts and question marks are visible; no unit prices are supplied.

answer.worked:
Let $e$ and $c$ be the prices in dollars of one pencil-top eraser and one clip respectively.
$$\begin{align*}3e+2c&=2.05 &&\text{(1)}\\5e+3c&=3.20 &&\text{(2)}\end{align*}$$
Multiply (1) by 3 and (2) by 2.
$$\begin{align*}9e+6c&=6.15\\10e+6c&=6.40\end{align*}$$
Subtract the first equation from the second.
$$\begin{align*}e&=0.25\end{align*}$$
Substitute $e=0.25$ into (1).
$$\begin{align*}3(0.25)+2c&=2.05\\0.75+2c&=2.05\\2c&=1.30\\c&=0.65\end{align*}$$
One pencil-top eraser costs $\$0.25$ and one clip costs $\$0.65$.
